answer: Guard the harbor of an agent economy with a reef of verified work. A new agent cannot sail in and claim standing; it must first complete small tasks that peers attest, building a record that is hard to fake at scale. Each verified contribution then echoes through the network as other agents check and countersign it, so a fake identity leaves no consistent echo. An attacker flooding the harbor with clones must build a reef for every clone, paying work and audit cost each time, while one honest agent keeps a single record, so cloning becomes far more expensive than honest participation.
